title: Americans are negotiating different models of the good life through childrearing values, work time, remote work, and passion versus pay
source_unit: Economist/YouGov Polls, summarized by YouGov in R-E-S-P-E-C-T? What Americans value in kids and work
geography: United States; adult citizens, with age, ideology, education, gender, parenthood, and labor-force comparisons

denominator.unit: U.S. adult citizens in the Economist/YouGov poll summarized by the source

self_reliance_over_obedience.unit: percent preferring self-reliance over obedience for children

manners_over_curiosity.unit: percent preferring good manners over curiosity

elder_respect_over_independence.unit: percent preferring respect for elders over independence

ideological_socialization_split.value: Liberals more often choose self-reliance, consideration, curiosity, and independence; conservatives more often choose obedience, good manners, and respect for elders.

age_heritage_gap.value: 80% of adults 65+ prefer respect for elders over independence, versus 53% of adults under 30.

observations.method: Economist/YouGov opt-in-panel survey; sample stratified and weighted to U.S. adult citizens using demographic, region, voter-registration, and political targets.
observations.uncertainty: These are stated preference trade-offs, not observed parenting, child outcomes, intergenerational behavior, or causal effects of ideology and age.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adult citizens, with age, ideology, education, and gender comparisons reported by YouGov.
observations.counterinterpretation: Forced-choice wording may exaggerate contrasts between traits that respondents could value simultaneously in everyday life.

observations.period: September 11-14, 2026; ideal workweek for work-life balance

denominator.unit: U.S. adult citizens in the Economist/YouGov poll summarized by the source

under_35_hours.unit: percent saying a healthy work-life-balance workweek should be 35 hours or less

under_30_hours.unit: percent saying the normal workweek should be less than 30 hours

under_30_age_gap.value: 69% of adults under 30 prefer 35 hours or less, versus 36% of adults 65 and older.

ideology_time_gap.value: 75% of very liberal adults prefer a shorter workweek, versus 32% of very conservative adults.

time_meaning_route.value: Work-time preference is a cultural and political judgment about a healthy life, not only a labor-supply calculation.

observations.method: Economist/YouGov opt-in-panel survey with stratification and weighting described in the source methodology.
observations.uncertainty: Ideal hours do not establish actual hours, employer feasibility, income loss, productivity, care substitution, or policy support for a particular workweek law.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adult citizens by age and ideological self-placement.
observations.counterinterpretation: Shorter-workweek preferences may reflect current labor-market conditions, household resources, or survey framing rather than a durable cultural shift.

denominator.unit: U.S. adult citizens in the Economist/YouGov poll summarized by the source

remote_work_support.unit: percent strongly or somewhat supporting employers being required to let people work from home when the job can be done remotely

remote_work_opposition.unit: percent opposing such a remote-work requirement

parent_gender_education_pattern.value: Support is higher among parents of young children, women, college graduates, and liberals.

work_control_route.value: Remote work is treated as a legitimate condition of work-life balance, with access shaped by care, gender, education, and ideology.

observations.method: Economist/YouGov national public-opinion poll summarized in the source article; remote-work question concerns jobs that can be performed remotely.
observations.uncertainty: Stated support does not establish whether respondents' jobs are remote-capable, whether mandates are legally or operationally feasible, or how remote work affects productivity and care.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adult citizens, including parents of young children, women, college graduates, and ideological groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Support for remote work may represent a preference for flexibility rather than a general endorsement of employer mandates.

denominator.unit: U.S. adult citizens in the Economist/YouGov poll summarized by the source

passion_over_pay.unit: percent preferring a passionate job over a well-paying job

pay_over_passion.unit: percent preferring a well-paying job over a passionate job

full_time_passion.unit: percent of full-time workers prioritizing passion over pay

nonworker_passion.value: Passion over pay rises to 53% among part-time workers, 56% among unemployed adults, and 58% among retirees.

success_model_route.value: The meaning of a good job is split between economic security and identity/purpose, and the balance changes with labor-force position and age.

observations.method: Economist/YouGov public-opinion poll summarized by YouGov; source reports labor-force subgroup comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: A forced choice between passion and pay does not measure actual job choice, income needs, job quality, or long-term wellbeing.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adult citizens by full-time, part-time, unemployed, retired, age, and education status.
observations.counterinterpretation: People may answer aspirationally, while household costs and labor-market constraints determine actual employment decisions.

related_sources.claim: The official YouGov summary provides the child-trait trade-offs, age/ideology/education/gender comparisons, workweek preferences, remote-work support, passion-versus-pay split, poll waves, and methodology.
Economist/YouGov poll toplines and crosstabs provide the underlying poll tables linked by the source article.

boundary: This record adds a social-reproduction and work-meaning route: childrearing ideals, work time, remote-work legitimacy, and passion-versus-pay choices are patterned by age, ideology, education, parenthood, and labor-force position. It does not establish actual parenting, work hours, remote-work access, earnings, policy effects, or durable value change.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official YouGov article was reviewed for the two poll waves, child-trait comparisons, workweek distributions, remote-work support, passion-versus-pay comparisons, subgroup patterns, and methodology.
